ety.text: Possibly borrowed from Polish wiarołomny, itself possibly a calque of German treubrüchig. First attested in 1717. Compare Ukrainian віроло́мний (virolómnyj), Belarusian верало́мны (vjeralómny), Bulgarian and Macedonian вероломен (verolomen).

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic истѧѕати (istędzati). By surface analysis, ис- (is-) + -тяза́ть (-tjazátʹ) (akin to тяга́ть (tjagátʹ), via PIE akin to тяну́ть (tjanútʹ)).
